mcq.q: India needs 10 labour-hours for a unit of cloth and 15 for a unit of wine; Portugal needs 12 for cloth and 8 for wine. India has a comparative advantage in cloth because its opportunity cost of cloth (in units of wine) is only:
mcq.explain: In India, one unit of cloth costs 10 hours, which could produce 10 ÷ 15 = 0.67 unit of wine; in Portugal, cloth costs 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 units of wine. India gives up less wine for each unit of cloth, so it has a comparative advantage in cloth, and Portugal in wine.
mcq.fast: Opportunity cost of cloth = hours for cloth ÷ hours for wine; lower = comparative advantage.

mcq.q: A country that can produce a good with fewer resources than another country has, according to Adam Smith, an:
mcq.explain: Adam Smith argued that each country should specialise in goods it can produce more efficiently, using fewer resources, than other countries — an absolute advantage — and trade for the rest. David Ricardo later showed that trade is beneficial even without absolute advantage, on the basis of comparative advantage.
mcq.fast: Fewer resources than rival = absolute advantage (Smith).

mcq.q: Country Z has plenty of labour but little capital. According to the Heckscher–Ohlin theory, Z will mainly export:
options: Labour-intensive goods such as ready-made garments
mcq.explain: The Heckscher–Ohlin (factor endowment) theory says countries differ in their relative endowments of factors. A country exports goods that use intensively its abundant, and therefore cheap, factor, and imports goods that use its scarce factor. A labour-abundant country thus exports labour-intensive goods like garments.
mcq.fast: Export what uses your abundant factor.

mcq.q: Mercantilists believed that a nation becomes rich mainly by:
options: Maximising exports, restricting imports and accumulating gold and silver
mcq.explain: Mercantilism, dominant in Europe from the 16th to 18th centuries, measured national wealth by stocks of gold and silver. It favoured a trade surplus — more exports and fewer imports — and supported tariffs, colonies and state regulation. Adam Smith and later classical economists criticised this view.
mcq.topic: Mercantilism — trade as a way to pile up gold

mcq.q: The "new trade theory" explains trade between similar countries mainly by:
options: Economies of scale and consumers' demand for product variety
mcq.explain: New trade theory, associated with Paul Krugman, explains why similar countries trade similar goods, such as cars. Firms gain economies of scale by producing for a large global market, and consumers like variety, so each country specialises in certain varieties and trades with others.
mcq.topic: New trade theory — scale, variety and network effects
mcq.fast: Similar countries, similar goods -> scale economies + variety (Krugman).

mcq.q: Gottfried Haberler restated Ricardo's comparative advantage theory in terms of:
mcq.explain: Ricardo's theory rested on the labour theory of value. Haberler restated comparative advantage in terms of opportunity cost — the amount of one good given up to produce another — which does not depend on labour being the only factor. This made the theory more general and realistic.
